title: The core physics and its 2D test view behind my sailing game, built with Claude
author: GoneSailingDev
selftext:
Hey all,

here's the first version of my sailing game. On day 1 I focused only on the physics: a standalone library with just the sailing logic, plus an interactive 2D top-down view to test it.

That was the foundation for the 3D version I posted earlier. The 3D game uses the same physics library that is behind this 2D view.

In the video you can see a 30 ft cruiser sailing upwind, tacking, and then turning downwind. The blue arrow is the true wind. The cyan arrow is the apparent wind, the wind the boat actually feels. The sail colors show whether the air flows smoothly along the sail or not.

About the AI part: Claude researched, wrote and tested this physics library. A key point: it measured things instead of just assuming them. Three examples:

* Before any physics code existed, Claude set a speed target range for the boat, based on published boat tests and published hull measurements, and froze it. The physics has to stay inside this range, and an automatic test checks that.
* Its first model for wave drag made the boat sail backwards in short waves. A test in the sim showed this, so the model was replaced with one based on published research data for yacht hulls.
* The 3D hull didn't match the data the physics used. The mismatch was found, the hull was reshaped, and the export now stops if the hull drifts away from the data again.

The 2D view is a testing tool for me, not the game itself.
